shared_elements: shallow/low-relief carving cut into coarse weathered stone
horizontal banding of the carved field into registers or belts
justification: Both are monumental weathered stone surfaces bearing shallow incised/low-relief motifs organised in broadly horizontal bands, and both include ring or disc-like elements, which is about the extent of the correspondence. The decisive difference is format and manner: A is a flat vertical rock face covered with dense rows of small linear signs and eroded figures set within a quarried architectural surface, while B is a free-standing three-dimensional carved figure whose curved back carries a few large, sparse, boldly modelled curvilinear devices.
